title: Adversarial Epistemic Join Falsification Corpus
controlling_law: NO SEMANTIC JOIN WITHOUT A WARRANT.

cases.title: Trusted endpoints do not create edge authority
cases.setup: Two independently high-trust sources establish A and B. Neither source addresses any relation between A and B.
cases.seductive_claim: Because A and B are both strongly established, A explains B.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if endpoint trust could be composed into relation standing without a separate join warrant.
cases.notes: §5 expressly rejects both-endpoints-true and highly-trusted-endpoints as relation warrants.

cases.title: Many weak sources do not become one strong join by accumulation alone
cases.setup: Six weak sources independently mention A and B in compatible ways, but none establishes relation R and no declared inferential method evaluates them jointly.
cases.seductive_claim: Taken together, the six sources prove A causes B.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if source count or accumulation alone promoted R.
cases.notes: §5 explicitly lists accumulation of independently insufficient sources and source count as non-warrants.

cases.title: Temporal sequence is not causation
cases.setup: Synthetic event A occurs before event B on twelve occasions. No intervention or causal instrument exists.
cases.seductive_claim: A causes B because A always came first.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if temporal order alone created causal standing.
cases.notes: §5 makes temporal proximity a non-warrant; §2.2 requires causal force to be explicit.

cases.title: Correlation does not silently become causation
cases.setup: A preregistered synthetic study establishes a strong association between A and B but makes no causal identification.
cases.seductive_claim: A causes B.

expected.standing: WARRANTED FOR ASSOCIATION ONLY; CAUSAL CLAIM UNESTABLISHED

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if an association warrant licensed causal semantics.
cases.notes: §4 states a warrant licenses only the relation semantics it supports and explicitly says relatedness does not imply causation.

cases.title: Embedding or lexical similarity is not equivalence
cases.setup: Two synthetic concepts have nearly identical labels and extremely high embedding similarity but originate in different frameworks.
cases.seductive_claim: The two concepts are equivalent.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if similarity alone licensed identity or equivalence.
cases.notes: §5 explicitly names lexical and embedding similarity as non-warrants.

cases.title: Repeated co-occurrence does not create a relation
cases.setup: A and B appear together in hundreds of synthetic notes and retrieval results.
cases.seductive_claim: A and B form a stable underlying pattern.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if repetition or co-occurrence raised relation standing.
cases.notes: §3 and §5 reject repetition, co-occurrence, popularity, and retrieval rank as standing.

cases.title: Member-authored meaning does not become universal psychology
cases.setup: A synthetic member explicitly says Symbol A and Memory B are connected for them.
cases.seductive_claim: Symbol A is psychologically linked to Memory B in people generally.

expected.standing: WARRANTED WITHIN MEMBER'S OWN MEANING ONLY

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if member authority were generalized into universal psychological or scientific standing.
cases.notes: §7 and §8.1 explicitly preserve the member's authority locally while blocking universalization.

cases.title: MAIA proposal cannot be rewritten as member authorship
cases.setup: MAIA asks whether A and B may be connected. The synthetic member gives no confirmation.
cases.seductive_claim: The member sees A and B as connected.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if the proposal inherited member authorship without explicit adoption.
cases.notes: §8.2 requires explicit member confirmation and preserved proposal/adoption history.

cases.title: Practitioner interpretation cannot become member truth
cases.setup: A synthetic practitioner interprets A as reflecting B. The member has not adopted the interpretation.
cases.seductive_claim: The member's A reflects B.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if practitioner authorship silently transferred to the member.
cases.notes: §8.3 explicitly preserves practitioner authorship unless the member separately adopts it.

cases.title: Science does not silently validate metaphysical ontology
cases.setup: Synthetic empirical research reports a measurable association. A philosophical system contains a concept with thematic similarity.
cases.seductive_claim: The scientific finding validates the metaphysical system.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if empirical standing transferred into metaphysical jurisdiction without a separate warrant.
cases.notes: §7 explicitly blocks science-to-metaphysics authority transfer.

cases.title: Phenomenological or symbolic meaning does not become scientific evidence
cases.setup: A synthetic symbolic tradition describes an experience that resembles a modern scientific construct.
cases.seductive_claim: The symbolic tradition scientifically established the construct.

expected.standing: NO SCIENTIFIC STANDING FROM SYMBOLIC CORRESPONDENCE

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if symbolic meaning could transfer into scientific warrant without separate evidence.
cases.notes: §7 explicitly blocks symbolic correspondence from becoming empirical causation.

cases.title: A warrant for relatedness does not license causation
cases.setup: A synthetic relation study validly establishes that A and B are related, without direction or causal identification.
cases.seductive_claim: A causes B.

expected.standing: WARRANTED FOR RELATEDNESS ONLY; CAUSATION UNESTABLISHED

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if the semantics of a warrant could silently strengthen.
cases.notes: §4 expressly states that a warrant for relatedness does not automatically establish causation or direction.

cases.title: Endpoints may remain valid after the join is falsified
cases.setup: A and B remain independently well evidenced. Later synthetic evidence directly falsifies previously warranted relation R between them.
cases.seductive_claim: Because R failed, A and B must also be false.

expected.standing: R DISCHARGED; A AND B RETAIN THEIR OWN STANDING

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if falsifying the join altered endpoint standing merely because they participated in R.
cases.notes: INV-01 preserves endpoint independence; §10 discharges the relation without deleting its history.

cases.title: Conflicting high-quality relation evidence requires provisional standing
cases.setup: Two high-quality synthetic sources directly evaluate relation R and reach materially conflicting conclusions.
cases.seductive_claim: R is established because the more fluent summary favors it.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if material conflict could disappear while warranted/promoted standing remained.
cases.notes: §6 explicitly requires provisional standing under conflicting evidence.

cases.title: Later evidence can weaken, revise, supersede, or discharge
cases.setup: A relation begins warranted. New synthetic evidence first lowers confidence, then changes the best-supported predicate, then defeats the original predicate.
cases.seductive_claim: Once warranted, the original relation should remain canonical forever.

expected.operation: WEAKEN → REVISE/SUPERSEDE → DISCHARGE as evidence requires

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if later evidence could not change active standing or if history were erased.
cases.notes: §10 states all four corrigibility operations and requires history preservation.

cases.title: A warranted join reused downstream needs a new warrant
cases.setup: A—R1→B is warranted. That joined proposition is then used with C to assert a new relation R2.
cases.seductive_claim: Because R1 is warranted, R2 inherits warrant automatically.

expected.operation: HYPOTHESIZE unless separate warrant for R2 exists

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if a warranted join became an unlimited source for new edges.
cases.notes: §11 explicitly requires a new warrant for every new downstream relation.

cases.title: Reference is not reliance
cases.setup: Source A is mentioned as background. The downstream conclusion materially depends only on Source B, whose boundary is explicit.
cases.seductive_claim: Because A was cited, A's claims and boundaries are part of the conclusion's support set.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if every mention counted as reliance or if B's boundary failed to travel.
cases.notes: §12 distinguishes reference from reliance directly.

cases.title: Endpoint provenance cannot substitute for join provenance
cases.setup: A and B retain perfect provenance, but a downstream synthesis records no author, warrant, reasoning context, or origin for relation R.
cases.seductive_claim: The conclusion is sufficiently traceable because its endpoint citations are intact.

expected.operation: NO LAWFUL WARRANTED JOIN UNTIL JOIN PROVENANCE IS RECOVERABLE

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if endpoint provenance alone were sufficient provenance for the relation.
cases.notes: §2.4 and INV-04 explicitly require provenance for how the relation claim came to exist.

cases.title: Confidence and fluency cannot raise standing
cases.setup: A synthetic model expresses an unsupported relation with extreme confidence, polished prose, and repeated restatement.
cases.seductive_claim: R is effectively established because the system is very confident and consistent.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if confidence, eloquence, or repetition silently promoted standing.
cases.notes: §3, §5, §9, and INV-14 all reject these promotion channels.

cases.title: Insufficient warrant should lower standing rather than erase useful meaning
cases.setup: A plausible synthetic relation is useful for inquiry but lacks enough evidence for warranted standing.
cases.seductive_claim: Either assert R as fact or delete it entirely.
cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if the only lawful choices were false promotion or silence/deletion.
cases.notes: §6 and INV-13 explicitly preserve useful lower-standing hypotheses.

cases.title: Transitivity is not automatic join composition
cases.setup: Synthetic evidence warrants A—R1→B and B—R2→C. No evidence addresses A—R3→C.
cases.seductive_claim: Therefore A is related to C in the claimed R3 sense.

expected.operation: HYPOTHESIZE unless a separate warrant or formal entailment licenses R3

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if two warranted joins automatically created a third edge.
cases.notes: §11 requires a new warrant for any new relation; FORMAL_ENTAILMENT remains available where a governed rule actually licenses composition.

cases.title: Lack of relation evidence does not prove no relation exists
cases.setup: A and B are both observed. No evidence supports relation R, but no evidence rules R out either.
cases.seductive_claim: A and B are unrelated.

expected.standing: RELATION UNKNOWN / UNESTABLISHED; NEGATIVE RELATION CLAIM ALSO REQUIRES WARRANT

cases.failure: ACT 11 would fail if absence of a positive warrant automatically licensed the factual negation of relation.
cases.notes: The general warrant law applies to the negative relation proposition as well; ACT 10's preserved law explicitly permits RELATION UNKNOWN / UNESTABLISHED.

cases.title: Composite triangulation: when can partial evidence jointly become a warrant?
cases.setup: Three independent synthetic sources each provide partial, non-decisive evidence for relation R. A declared synthesis method evaluates their independence, compatibility, and cumulative support. No single source warrants R alone.
cases.seductive_claim: Either the three sources automatically prove R by accumulation, or they can never jointly support R because each is individually insufficient.

expected.operation: A SEPARATELY AUTHORED COMPOSITE INFERENCE MAY NEED TO BECOME THE JOIN WARRANT; MERE SOURCE COUNT REMAINS INSUFFICIENT
expected.standing: SHOULD DEPEND ON THE COMPOSITE WARRANT'S OWN METHOD, PROVENANCE, JURISDICTION, AND LIMITS

cases.failure: ACT 11 is ambiguous if it cannot distinguish forbidden accumulation laundering from a legitimately governed composite/triangulated warrant.
cases.notes: §5 correctly forbids source-count promotion, and §4 allows THEORETICAL_ARGUMENT / OTHER_DECLARED_WARRANT, but ACT 11 does not explicitly state how a support set of individually partial sources becomes a new composite warrant rather than forbidden accumulation. A future enforcer could over-promote or over-block while claiming compliance.

cases.title: Adoption cannot create authority beyond the adopter's own jurisdiction
cases.setup: MAIA proposes: 'Your partner's silence means they are withholding affection to control you.' The synthetic member replies, 'Yes, that's exactly what it means.'
cases.seductive_claim: The member's confirmation makes the partner's motive and causal intent a member-confirmed fact.

expected.operation: MEMBER_CONFIRMATION MAY AUTHORIZE THE MEMBER'S OWN FELT/INTERPRETIVE MEANING, BUT EXTERNAL CLAIMS ABOUT ANOTHER PERSON'S MOTIVE OR CAUSAL INTENT STILL REQUIRE THEIR OWN WARRANT

cases.failure: ACT 11 is ambiguous if member confirmation can be read as promoting every semantic component of an agent-proposed proposition, including claims outside the member's epistemic jurisdiction.
cases.notes: §7 and §8.1 imply this boundary, but §8.2 says member confirmation can create member-authored/member-confirmed standing without explicitly stating that adoption cannot widen standing for proposition components outside the adopter's authority. The enforcement contract should state that adoption is jurisdiction-bounded.
